**Sikhae (Seafood Stew) – A Quick & Easy Guide** > *“Sik”* means “seafood,” while *“hae”* refers to a spicy stew style common in Korean households. > It’s perfect for quick week‑night dinners because you only need one pot. --- ### Ingredients | Category | Item(s) | |-------------------|-----------------------------------------| | **Base** | 1 L water / seafood stock | | **Seasonings** | • Gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes)
• Soy sauce
• Salt/pepper
• Sesame oil (optional)
• Garlic (minced) | | **Vegetables** | • Onion (sliced)
• Green onion (cut into bite‑size pieces)
• Carrot (julienned)
• Zucchini (thinly sliced) | | **Protein** | • Shrimp (peeled, deveined)
• Squid (cleaned, cut into rings)
• Clams or mussels (washed)
• Fish fillets (like cod or pollock, cubed) | | **Optional Extras** | • Tofu cubes
• Kimchi (small amount, optional) | *(Feel free to mix-and-match according to what’s fresh at your kitchen.)* --- ### Equipment Needed - One medium-sized pot or Dutch oven - Knife + cutting board - Stirring spoon --- ### Step-by-Step Instructions #### 1️⃣ Prep Your Seafood - Rinse all shellfish under cold running water; pat dry with paper towels. - If using clams/mussels, soak them briefly in salted water to help open them later. #### 2️⃣ Make the Base Broth 1. In the pot, bring 1 L of water or pre-made seafood stock to a gentle boil. 2. Add minced garlic (about 1 tbsp). Let it simmer for ~5 minutes so flavors infuse. #### 3️⃣ Layer Vegetables - Toss in onions, carrots, zucchini, and green onions. - Cook until they’re just tender (~3–4 min). #### 4️⃣ Season! - Sprinkle about 2–3 tsp of gochugaru over the veggies. Adjust if you prefer more heat. - Drizzle 1–2 tsp soy sauce and add salt/paper to taste. - Optional: stir in a splash of sesame oil for aroma. #### 5️⃣ Add the Seafoods - Drop shrimp first—cook for 1 minute before adding others. - Then add squid rings, fish cubes, and finally clams/mussels. - Cover and let everything steam together for 5–7 minutes until the shells open and proteins turn opaque. #### 6️⃣ Final Touches - Taste again; tweak seasoning if needed. - If you want extra depth, drop in tofu cubes now—they’ll absorb the broth nicely. - Optionally fold in a small handful of kimchi for tanginess. #### 7️⃣ Serve Immediately - Ladle hot stew straight from the pot onto bowls. - Garnish with chopped green onions or a drizzle of chili paste if desired. - Pair with steamed rice or a side salad for a balanced meal. --- ### Tips & Variations | Tip | Why It Helps | |-----|--------------| | Use a high-quality seafood stock instead of plain water → richer flavor. | | Keep an eye on the clams/mussels; once they crack open, remove immediately to avoid rubbery texture. | | For a milder version, reduce gochugaru to half a teaspoon or replace some with mild paprika. | | Add a pinch of sugar after opening clams to balance acidity. | | Leftover stew? Reheat gently; don’t boil too long or seafood will toughen. | Enjoy your homemade **Sikhae**—a comforting bowl brimming with oceanic goodness!
